svg.title: Aegis: persistent browser architecture
svg.desc: Source-backed architecture diagram. Agents and the aegis CLI send local HTTP requests to a persistent Rust server. The context manager serializes work through AegisRuntime and CefBridge. A C ABI connects to the native CEF host in the same process. CEF IPC connects the browser to its renderer, where window.__aegis inspects and acts on the real page DOM. Aegis JSON state, Aegis runtime traces, and Fozzy scenario traces have separate ownership.

svg.text: REAL BROWSER / SEMANTIC CONTROL / STRUCTURED STATE
One default runtime; named contexts are managed independently.
RESULTS + DOM CHANGES + EVENTS / collected and sequenced in Rust
Headless or headful; bootstrap is local
The shared library lives in the host process.
CEF messages cross the renderer boundary.
Role, name, label, text; document-local IDs
Session JSON, credentials, uploads, downloads, logs
$AEGIS_HOME overrides the root; atomic JSON writes
Chromium profile internals are runtime substrate.
JSON requests, responses, snapshots + sequenced events
Reconstructs snapshot + event state without CEF.
Separate from Aegis's JSON runtime trace format.
Route > serialize > execute > bridge > render > inspect / act
Source: aegis-architecture.json | boundary checks: server.rs, host ABI, aegis_app.cc, trace/recorder.rs
